title: EXP-088 - Hello World Part 5 Section 9: Create the FX_CustomerID Component Class (Validator, Validate Immediately, List Source)
objective: Follow hello-world-pt5.md Section 9 (13:06-15:08), adapted to FX_ names and User scope. Through the Web Designer Edit > Component Class global-object dialog (docs/mongoose/guides/web-designer.md "Creating a Component Class object"), create one Component Class: Name FX_CustomerID; Data Source > Validation > Validators: FX_CustomerID with Parameters %1,%2; Validate Immediately True; List Source: Type IDO Collection, IDO FX_HelloWorld01, Properties FX_Code, FX_Label, FX_Address, Columns to Display FX_Code and FX_Label. The validator FX_CustomerID was created in EXP-087 (In Collection on FX_HelloWorld01, outputs %1 = FX_Label and %2 = FX_Address); the class forwards its own %1,%2 parameters to it. FX_Address is fetched by the list source but not displayed, so a drop-down choice can feed the validator output. Commit every field with Tab before OK. Read the class back, perform one Designer Save, close and reopen the FX_Orders Designer Form once and read it back again. Applying the class to the FX_Orders combobox and grid column is Section 10 (EXP-089); the tutorial's cache step is deferred to the runtime test. Findings are observed only.

in_scope: Read AGENTS.md, docs/mongoose/transcripts/hello-world-pt5.md Sections 9-10 and their transcript lines (13:06-16:22), docs/mongoose/guides/web-designer.md ("Creating a Component Class object"), docs/mongoose/guides/global-objects-additional.md ("Modifying global objects in the Web Designer"), the EXP-087 record and outcome (the Global Objects dialog, the validator values, Tab commits, Cancel readbacks, the Save toast), the EXP-085 outcome and the EXP-064 outcome (Global Objects editors, OK then OK then Save) before browser interaction.
Create or update only experiments/EXP-088-hello-world-part-5-section-9-fx-customerid-component-class.md and evidence/EXP-088/ documentation and evidence files.
Record the worker-written-file inventory and a cumulative browser action audit with exact counts.

Use the existing authenticated session without refresh, restart or configuration change. If it expires, follow the worker-preamble session-expiry procedure once and end the task; never sign in inside the portal's embedded app frame (refused, EXP-080-R2) but use the procedure's top-level portal navigation. List the browser tabs before the first tab selection. Answer any prompt within the same task; never leave a prompt or dialog open across tasks unless the coordinator's next task explicitly continues it. After any pause, inspect the state read-only before acting and never replay an earlier action.

Preflight and gates: the Designer is in User scope and clean with FX_Orders open (open it once through the Form menu recent-forms entry if needed). Open Designer Edit > Component Class once read-only, record the dialog layout (list, list controls, Properties pane, buttons) and whether FX_CustomerID exists in the Component Classes list, and close it with its Cancel control. Open Edit > Validator once read-only, confirm FX_CustomerID is present with Type In Collection, and close it with Cancel. If the component class FX_CustomerID already exists, or the validator is missing, record it and stop blocked without creating anything.

Creation: open Edit > Component Class once, use the list New (+) control once, enter the Name FX_CustomerID, confirm the name prompt with its OK once, and record the new property sheet (its groups and the Data Source > Validation rows).

Validator: under Data Source > Validation open the Validators ellipsis once, record the editor layout, use its Add control once and choose the validator FX_CustomerID; with that validator selected open its Parameters control once, enter %1,%2 exactly, commit and verify, and confirm with OK once; confirm the validators editor with OK once. Set Validate Immediately to True (choose from its list, Tab once, verify).

List Source: open the List Source ellipsis once and record the dialog layout. Set Type IDO Collection and IDO FX_HelloWorld01 (choose each from its list, or type the exact IDO name if the list is empty; Tab and verify). Open the Properties ellipsis once, add FX_Code, FX_Label and FX_Address in that order, verify, and OK once. Open the Columns to Display control once, select FX_Code and FX_Label only (Shift- or Ctrl-click as the picker requires), verify FX_Address is not selected, and OK once. Record the list source value verbatim if the dialog or property sheet shows one, then confirm the List Source dialog with OK once.
Confirm the Global Objects dialog with OK once; record each dialog response and whether the Designer Save became enabled.
String or message stop rule: if any prompt offers to create a string or message, answer No once and record it; never create one.

Readback: open Edit > Component Class once, select FX_CustomerID, record every visible property set in this experiment (the Validators value, Validate Immediately and the List Source value verbatim; open an ellipsis read-only only if a value is not fully visible, and close it with Cancel), and close the dialog with Cancel.

Correction contingency, at most once and only for a value that reads blank or wrong: in that dialog select FX_CustomerID, correct only that value (commit with Tab, verify), confirm with OK, and repeat the readback once.
Perform exactly one Designer Save through the native toolbar Save and record the native response verbatim; if Save is disabled at that point, record it and make no Save.

Close the clean FX_Orders Designer Form once through its Form-tab control and reopen it once through the Form menu recent-forms entry; read FX_CustomerID back once more through Edit > Component Class (closing with Cancel); confirm no FX_Orders component changed (the Designer stays clean).

Capture screenshots of the gate lists, the new property sheet, the validators editor with the parameters before OK, Validate Immediately, the List Source dialog with Type and IDO, the Properties and Columns to Display selections before OK, each readback, the Save and the reopened readback.
Record any blocker after at most one fresh untargeted snapshot and one corrected visible inspection. Classify findings as observed only.

Component class FX_CustomerID created once through New; validator FX_CustomerID added once with Parameters %1,%2; Validate Immediately True; List Source Type IDO Collection, IDO FX_HelloWorld01, Properties FX_Code, FX_Label, FX_Address, Columns to Display FX_Code and FX_Label only; each value committed before OK and each dialog confirmed once. Evidence: dialog screenshots before each OK.

The readback shows the validator with %1,%2, Validate Immediately True and the List Source verbatim with FX_HelloWorld01, the three properties and the two displayed columns (corrections, if any, within the contingency); exactly one Designer Save with its native response, or Save disabled recorded. Evidence: readback and Save screenshots.
The clean Form closed once and reopened once; the reopened readback matches AC-3; no component changed; no validator or other class changed. Evidence: reopen readback screenshots.

The final EXP-088 report gives decisive evidence for AC-1 to AC-4, the complete action audit with exact counts (component classes created 1, New 1, validators added 1, list-source properties 3, displayed columns 2, dialog OKs, Tab commits, string prompts and answers, contingency corrections, Designer Save at most 1, Designer close/reopen 1, zero component changes, zero runtime actions, zero checkout actions, re-login count), the worker-written-file inventory and the final state. Repository confinement is supported by worker/harness inventories, with operator git review authoritative. Findings are observed only.
